name: Strait of Dover
note: The narrowest point of the Channel — the far coast is visible on a clear day.
description: The Strait of Dover is the busiest seaway in the world and the narrowest point of the English Channel — about thirty-three kilometres of grey water between the white cliffs of England and the French coast, plainly visible from each other on a clear day. Hundreds of vessels pass through daily, crossed at right angles by ferries shuttling between Dover and Calais, all of it managed by the world's first traffic separation scheme. The strait has been a moat and a bridge by turns: the Armada fought past it, Blériot flew it, Webb swam it, and since 1994 the Channel Tunnel has run beneath it.
